data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 defends the panel but conflates 'variance reduction' with reliability for tasks with objectively verifiable outcomes. A panel can have a narrow error distribution and still be systematically biased toward the wrong answer; lower variance around a miscalibrated mean is not greater reliability. Its own countercondition (shared systemic bias in the checklist) is acknowledged yet never operationalized: the target gives no within-evaluation evidence that would separate a genuine accuracy gain from a low-variance compliance process that happens to be wrong in the same direction.
